title: Dryer House Worksheet: Pricing One Pass of Stored Grain
content:
The pass is worked out on the moisture the scale read in when the grain was taken into store, on the bushels the most recent load into store was taken in on, at the programme's rate for each point of moisture on each bushel, and the grain is run down to the programme's target moisture. This worksheet covers Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements.

## The three quantities

**The points removed.** The points removed are the moisture the grain started the pass at less the moisture it is being run down to, carried to one decimal place, and a pass that would take out fewer than the programme's minimum points is billed at the minimum points rather than not at all.

**The bushels.** The bushels the pass is charged on are the bushels the most recent load into store was taken in on.

**The rate.** The rate applied is the programme's rate for each point of moisture on each bushel, carried to five decimal places before it is applied.

## The charge

The charge for the pass is the programme's rate for each point of moisture on each bushel through the dryer, multiplied by the points removed and by the bushels the pass was run on, that product rounded to the nearest cent; where what is left after any allowance falls under the programme's pass minimum the pass minimum is charged instead. An allowance is worked out on the charge for the pass and on nothing else, rounded to the nearest cent, and is taken off before the programme's pass minimum is applied.

## Worked pass, on hypothetical figures

Take a programme whose rate is 0.0470 for each point on each bushel, whose target moisture is 15.5 percent, whose minimum points are 0.5 and whose pass minimum is 18.00. The scale read the grain in at 19.2 percent when it was taken into store, and the most recent load into store was taken in on 7400 bushels.

1. The points removed are 19.2 less 15.5, which is 3.7, carried to one decimal place; 3.7 stands above the minimum points of 0.5, so 3.7 is what is billed.
2. The rate carried to five decimal places is 0.04700.
3. The charge is 0.04700 multiplied by 3.7 points multiplied by 7400 bushels, which is 1286.86 rounded to the nearest cent.
4. That figure stands above the pass minimum of 18.00, so 1286.86 is charged.

## A second hypothetical, where the floor governs

On the same programme, grain read in at 15.7 percent stands 0.2 of a point above the target of 15.5 percent. Two tenths is fewer than the minimum points of 0.5, so the pass is billed on 0.5 points. On 600 bushels the charge is 0.04700 multiplied by 0.5 points multiplied by 600 bushels, which is 14.10; that falls under the pass minimum of 18.00, so 18.00 is charged.
